arguments.summary: Audit identifies one material framing issue: the draft correctly labels company grids as hypothetical, but its decision-boundary claim nevertheless treats NVDA’s mechanically favorable grid asymmetry as constructive evidence. The asymmetry is generated by unvalidated, jointly selected EPS and P/E stress inputs and cannot support a comparative preference absent an empirical rationale for the ranges or a robustness test.

claims.text: The NVDA and MU scenario grids explicitly state that their annual EPS and P/E inputs are analyst assumptions rather than observed multiples, consensus, probabilities, targets, or fair values. NVDA’s larger bull-versus-bear asymmetry and MU’s near symmetry are therefore mechanical outputs of the selected joint EPS/P/E cases, not independently observed valuation evidence.

gaps.description: No observed company multiple, multiple history, consensus, or independent empirical rationale for the chosen 20x/24x/28x NVDA and 11x/14x/17x MU P/E bands is supplied. This does not invalidate clearly labelled sensitivity math, but it limits use of scenario asymmetry as evidence for a comparative preference.

assumptions: The director draft is evaluated only against the supplied fixed evidence and its own stated scenario qualifications.
A scenario grid remains useful to show conditional break-even and sensitivity even when it cannot establish a fair-value or directional ranking.
arguments.counter_thesis: If the Director presents the asymmetry solely as a transparent illustration of stipulated cases—not as a positive valuation feature or support for preference—the underlying grids and event-based review conditions remain sound.

review_conditions.description: Before relying on grid asymmetry in a relative conclusion, review whether an empirical issuer-specific multiple range or a robustness analysis with independently justified EPS and multiple stresses is available. If not, retain the grids only as conditional sensitivities and remove favorable/unfavorable asymmetry from preference reasoning.

objections.description: The claim describes NVDA’s “constructive grid asymmetry” as relevant to the conditional distinction. But the bull gain and bear loss result from coupled, unvalidated assumptions ($8/$10/$12 with 20x/24x/28x) rather than an observed valuation distribution or independently grounded downside/upside range. The grid itself disclaims such support. Retain it as sensitivity, but do not use favorable asymmetry as positive evidence in any NVDA-versus-MU-or-QQQ preference framing unless the Director supplies a non-arbitrary range rationale or demonstrates the conclusion is robust to alternative joint stresses.
